title: Interview Playbook
objectives: Explain Interview Playbook with measurable requirements and failure modes
Apply Interview Playbook to a high-traffic India-scale scenario in an interview

cards.title: 45-minute map
cards.body: Spend ~5m clarifying, ~10m estimation, ~15m high-level design, ~10m deep dive, ~5m trade-offs and wrap-up.

cards.title: Drive the whiteboard
cards.body: Label sync vs async paths, data stores, and queues. Narrate failure modes while you draw—not after.

cards.title: Checklist flow
cards.body: Requirements → numbers → API sketch → architecture → hot path → risks → trade-offs.

cards.title: Signals interviewers want
cards.body: Clear scope, realistic math, idempotent writes, observability, and explicit consistency/latency choices.

cards.title: Closing script
cards.body: Summarize bottlenecks, metrics, and what you would prototype in week one.

questions.explanation: Strong interviews anchor on requirements and SLOs before components.

questions.prompt: [spot074] Interview Playbook: during a 6× launch spike, which node saturates first on the dominant path? Ref interviewplaybookspot0074.
questions.explanation: Unsharded OLTP primaries usually exhaust connections/IOPS before stateless tiers.

questions.explanation: Numbers before boxes keeps trade-offs honest.

questions.prompt: [est074] Interview Playbook: assume 10,002,046 uniform reads/day — integer average read QPS. Key interviewplaybookest0074.
questions.explanation: Convert daily volume to per-second capacity before sizing caches and DB pools.

questions.prompt: [trade074] Interview Playbook: choose scaling posture for 6× lunch peak with multi-AZ survival and bounded staleness. Ref interviewplaybooktrade0074.

rationaleOptions.label: Stateless tiers absorb burst without one machine ceiling
Caching shifts read load off the primary
Vertical scale cannot survive AZ loss by itself

questions.explanation: Horizontal stateless scaling plus caching is the common interview answer for read-heavy bursts.

questions.prompt: [mc2074] For Interview Playbook, which non-functional facet (compliance lens) dominates revenue or safety risk in production? Tag interviewplaybookmc20074.

choices.label: Correctness under retries and partial failures

questions.explanation: Distributed systems fail partially; interviews probe how you preserve invariants.

flashcards.front: What is the core interview takeaway for Interview Playbook?
flashcards.back: Connect user journeys to SLOs, then justify components and trade-offs for Interview Playbook.

flashcards.front: Name one pitfall when discussing Interview Playbook.
flashcards.back: Skipping scale numbers, ignoring retries/idempotency, or mixing AuthN with AuthZ.

flashcards.front: Which metric would you cite first for Interview Playbook?
flashcards.back: p95 latency on the hot path plus error rate on writes/reads that affect revenue or safety.
